title: Neighbourhood Services and Community Resources
objectives: Identify and locate key neighbourhood services including libraries, community centres, and food banks
Ask for and provide information about local services using formal and informal registers
Describe your neighbourhood and its amenities using descriptive language
Evaluate whether a neighbourhood meets a family's needs by comparing available services

reading_passage.title: Finding Your Community in a New City
reading_passage.text:
Moving into a new neighbourhood is more than finding an apartment — it is about building a support network and learning where to access the services your family needs. For newcomers, this process can take months, and the learning often happens through word of mouth, through neighbours and coworkers, and through community organisations that specifically serve immigrant populations.

Most Portland neighbourhoods have a library branch within a short bus ride. Libraries are among the most accessible public resources: they are free, open to all residents regardless of immigration status, and offer far more than books. Many branches host English conversation groups, computer classes, children's storytime, and assistance with job applications. A library card is free and can be obtained with proof of a local address.

Food pantries and community meals are also widely available in Portland. Organisations such as Oregon Food Bank and Blanchet House operate distribution sites throughout the city. Many religious institutions — mosques, churches, and temples — also run weekly food programmes that serve anyone in need, often regardless of religious affiliation.

For families with children, knowing the location of the nearest park and school is essential. Portland Parks and Recreation operates more than 200 parks and offers subsidised recreation programmes for low-income families. Many community centres also provide after-school care, summer programmes, and English classes for adults. Making use of these services early helps families establish routines, meet neighbours, and reduce the isolation that many newcomers experience in their first months.
reading_passage.source: Adapted from the Welcome to Portland Newcomer Resource Guide, published by Immigrant and Refugee Community Organisation (IRCO), 2023

glossary.meaning: a group of people and services you can rely on for help and information
information passed from person to person through conversation, not through media
easy for people to reach or use, especially for those with few resources
a place where people can go to receive free food supplies
reduced in price because part of the cost is paid by the government or an organisation

comprehension.question: According to the passage, what services do Portland libraries offer besides lending books?
comprehension.answer: Libraries offer English conversation groups, computer classes, children's storytime, and assistance with job applications.

comprehension.question: What does the author imply when they say that food programmes serve people 'regardless of religious affiliation'?
comprehension.answer: The author implies that newcomers of any religion — or no religion — are welcome at these programmes, so they should not feel excluded or hesitant about going.

comprehension.question: What does 'subsidised' mean in paragraph four?
comprehension.answer: Reduced in price because part of the cost is covered by the government or an organisation — so low-income families pay less than the full price.

comprehension.question: Why does the author say newcomers should make use of neighbourhood services 'early'?
comprehension.answer: Because using community services early helps families build routines, meet neighbours, and reduce isolation — which is a significant challenge for many newcomers in their first months.

language_focus.title: Present Simple for Describing Regular Services and Facilities
language_focus.explanation: When describing neighbourhood services and how they work, we typically use the present simple tense. The present simple expresses facts, routines, and permanent arrangements — things that are generally true, not just happening right now. Notice that third-person singular subjects (the library, the food bank, the centre) take the -s form of the verb.

examples.sentence: The library opens at 9 AM on weekdays and offers free computer access.
examples.note: Both 'opens' and 'offers' use the third-person singular -s form because the subject is 'the library.'

examples.sentence: Many community centres provide after-school care and English classes for adults.
examples.note: 'Provide' does not take -s because the subject is plural — 'many community centres.'

practice.sentence: Complete with the correct form: 'The food bank ___ (distribute) supplies on Tuesday and Thursday afternoons.'
practice.answer: The food bank distributes supplies on Tuesday and Thursday afternoons.

practice.sentence: Correct the error: 'The library offer free English classes on Wednesday evenings.'
practice.answer: The library offers free English classes on Wednesday evenings. (Add -s for third-person singular.)

practice.sentence: Which is correct? A) Libraries is free for all residents. B) Libraries are free for all residents.
practice.answer: B) 'Libraries' is plural, so the verb must be 'are,' not 'is.'

vocabulary_in_context.definition: Easy to reach, use, or benefit from, particularly for people with limited resources
vocabulary_in_context.example_sentence: Libraries are among the most accessible public resources: they are free, open to all residents regardless of immigration status.

vocabulary_in_context.definition: A connection or membership with a particular group, organisation, or religion
vocabulary_in_context.example_sentence: Many religious institutions run weekly food programmes that serve anyone in need, often regardless of religious affiliation.

vocabulary_in_context.definition: The feeling of being alone and disconnected from other people and the community around you
vocabulary_in_context.example_sentence: Making use of these services early helps families reduce the isolation that many newcomers experience in their first months.

speaking_task.context: A newly arrived family in your neighbourhood has asked you for advice. They have two school-age children, they are learning English, and they are currently relying on food assistance.
speaking_task.prompt: Tell the family about three or four neighbourhood services that would help them most. Describe what each service offers, where to find it, and why it is relevant to their situation. Use the present simple tense to describe each service.
useful_language: The library on Division Street offers free English conversation groups on Tuesday mornings.
The food bank on Burnside distributes food on Tuesdays and Thursdays — you do not need to make an appointment.
The community centre provides after-school programmes for children aged 6 to 14.
speaking_task.model_answer: For a family in your situation, I would recommend starting with three places. First, the public library — it offers free English classes, children's activities, and computer access. You can get a free card with your address. Second, the Oregon Food Bank has a distribution site nearby — it opens on Tuesday and Thursday afternoons and you do not need an appointment. Third, the community centre on Foster Road provides after-school care and summer programmes for children at a subsidised cost. These three places will help your whole family settle in more quickly.

writing_workshop.model_text: My neighbourhood has several useful services that I use regularly. The library is about five minutes' walk from my building and opens at nine o'clock every day except Sunday. I go there on Wednesday evenings for an English conversation group, which meets in the meeting room on the first floor. There is also a food pantry at the mosque on 122nd Avenue that distributes food every Friday afternoon. It is free and open to everyone. These services make a real difference to families like mine who are still getting settled.
writing_workshop.model_analysis: Notice how the writer uses the present simple consistently to describe the services, includes specific details (times, days, locations), and ends with a personal reflection on why these services matter.
writing_workshop.task: Write about two or three neighbourhood services that you use or that are available to you. Describe what each service offers, when it is open, and how it has helped or could help you or your family.
success_criteria: Describe at least two different services using present simple tense throughout
Include specific details: days, times, or locations for at least one service
End with a personal reflection on why community services are important

quiz.question: According to the passage, what do you need to get a free library card in Portland?
options: A valid passport and proof of income
A social security number and photo ID
Proof of a local address
A referral from a resettlement agency
quiz.explanation: The passage says 'A library card is free and can be obtained with proof of a local address.'

quiz.question: What does the passage say about food programmes at religious institutions?
options: They are only available to members of that religion
They require a referral from a social worker
They serve anyone in need regardless of religious affiliation
They are only available on Sundays
quiz.explanation: The passage states 'many religious institutions run weekly food programmes that serve anyone in need, often regardless of religious affiliation.'

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly uses the present simple to describe a service?
options: The food bank are open on Tuesdays.
The food bank open on Tuesdays.
The food bank opens on Tuesdays.
The food bank is opening on Tuesdays.
quiz.explanation: 'Opens' is correct — the subject 'the food bank' is third-person singular and requires the -s ending in the present simple.

quiz.question: Why does the author say newcomers should use community services early, according to the final paragraph?
options: Because services often have waiting lists and spots fill up quickly
To help establish routines, meet neighbours, and reduce isolation
Because many services are only available to residents of less than one year
To demonstrate to immigration authorities that they are integrating
quiz.explanation: The passage says: 'Making use of these services early helps families establish routines, meet neighbours, and reduce the isolation that many newcomers experience in their first months.'

listening_exercises.transcript: The Northside Community Center is open Monday through Saturday, nine to nine. We offer free English classes on Tuesday and Thursday evenings, a food pantry on Wednesday mornings, and free help with taxes in the spring. The children's program runs after school until six. All services are free for neighborhood residents. Stop by the front desk to register.
listening_exercises.question: When are the free English classes?
options: Wednesday mornings
Tuesday and Thursday evenings
Every morning
Saturday at nine

listening_exercises.transcript: Your public library is much more than books. With a free library card, you can use computers and the internet, print documents, and borrow movies. Many libraries offer free classes for adults, story time for children, and quiet rooms for studying. Librarians can also help you find information about jobs, housing, and community services. Everything is free.
listening_exercises.question: What do you need to use library services?
options: A monthly payment
A free library card
A student ID
An appointment
